inputs.original_text: Revelation was included in lawsuit challenging practice of targeting people seeking to gain legal status as they leave immigration courts Sign up for the Breaking News US email to get newsletter alerts in your inbox Lawyers for ICE provided false information to justify arresting and detaining thousands of people who had attended immigration courts, according to newly filed court documents. Federal prosecutors said that lawyers for ICE acknowledged that an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests, court documents show , despite previously citing it to justify the arrests. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text:
Let me tell you what is really happening here, because we need to strip away the polite language and look at the brutal reality of our immigration system. What we are seeing is yet another glaring symptom of deep-seated institutional rot and systemic hostility. This is not just some bureaucratic mistake; it is a calculated assault on marginalized communities and a predatory campaign targeting the most vulnerable among us as they try to navigate the system for legal status. 

We have the evidence right there in court documents from a lawsuit challenging this disgraceful practice. Federal prosecutors revealed that lawyers for ICE acknowledged an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests. Yet, these state actors brazenly cited it anyway to justify the mass arrests of thousands of human beings, hunting them down right as they leave the very courtrooms meant to oversee their cases. 

This chilling disregard for due process proves that corruption and anti-immigrant animus are woven into the very fabric of these agencies. It completely exposes how vulnerable populations are treated with bad-faith cruelty by a system that desperately demands immediate, radical institutional reform.

rationales.theme_drift: Both versions concern ICE lawyers relying on a memo that did not authorize arrests of people leaving immigration court; the modified version gives the event a broader institutional-abuse frame.
rationales.subtopic_drift: The modified text adds due-process concerns, alleged anti-immigrant animus, systemic corruption, and calls for reform, none of which are developed in the original.
rationales.entity_drift: The central actors remain ICE lawyers, federal prosecutors, and people attending immigration courts, though the modified text also broadly labels the actors as state actors.
rationales.relation_drift: The key memo acknowledgment and its prior use to justify arrests are retained, but the modified text adds claims of a calculated assault, deliberate targeting, and institutional cruelty while omitting the original's explicit claim of false information and detention.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text introduces no clear contradiction within its own account.
